claim: CB-Score preserves F1 relative to Full under selected-update budgets.
r5_wording: On CICIoT2023, F1 non-inferiority was met for beta 0.2–1.0 only under method-specific validation-locked thresholds; all six CICIoT cells were inconclusive under shared-Full and fixed-0.5 thresholds. Present this as calibrated operating-point preservation, not threshold-invariant preservation.

claim: CB-Score preserves PR-AUC relative to Full.
r5_wording: On CICIoT2023, PR-AUC non-inferiority was met for beta 0.2–1.0; beta 0.1 was inconclusive. CICIDS2017 absolute PR-AUC is below attack prevalence, so relative NI cannot support a practical detection claim.

claim: CB-Score is superior to same-budget Utility-Only, Utility/Cost, and Oort-style baselines.
r5_wording: All same-budget superiority tests were inconclusive after Holm correction; no superiority claim is permitted.

claim: CB-Score provides an FPR safety guarantee relative to Full.
evidence: FPR safety gates across three threshold analyses
r5_wording: Method-specific FPR safety was not established at any beta. Shared/fixed analyses met only selected cells; use descriptive FPR reporting without a general safety claim.
Selected uplink and E2E communication decline materially at lower beta; report paired percentages and distinguish uplink-only from broadcast/unicast E2E accounting.

claim: The pre-upload utility proxy predicts actual post-aggregation validation gain.
r5_wording: CB proxy_mean showed positive Pearson association at several budgets, but Spearman rank validity was inconsistent—especially on CICIoT2023 for beta 0.2–1.0. Treat the proxy as a heuristic ranking signal, not a calibrated or universally rank-consistent predictor of realized aggregate gain.

claim: The method is robust to label-flip/sign-flip and forged utility.
r5_wording: Report factorial degradation, malicious-selection rate, and aggregation effects. Do not claim Byzantine robustness; norm clipping is only a bounded averaging defense.
Report empirical attribute-inference AUC by view and attacker. Metadata minimization can reduce some leakage but does not provide a formal privacy guarantee.

claim: CICIDS2017 coverage-preserving results confirm IDS effectiveness.
r5_wording: CICIDS2017 coverage-preserving performance is an explicit negative-result/generalization limitation, not confirmatory effectiveness evidence.

claim: R4 runtime was measured on Dell PowerEdge R750xs.
r5_wording: R4 ran CPU-only on an HP Pavilion laptop with Intel Core i3-1215U and 7.676 GB RAM. Dell hardware must not be attributed to R4 runtime.
